questions.question: If $Q_c > K_c$, in which direction will the reaction proceed to achieve equilibrium? (FBISE 2024-II)
questions.explanation: When the reaction quotient $Q_c$ is greater than the equilibrium constant $K_c$, there is an excess of products relative to reactants. Therefore, the reaction proceeds in the reverse direction (right to left) to re-establish equilibrium.

questions.question: For the reaction between phosphorus trichloride and chlorine to form phosphorus pentachloride ($PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_5(g)$), what is the unit of $K_c$? (FBISE 2020-I, 2021-I, 2024-I)
questions.explanation: For $PCl_3 + Cl_2 \rightleftharpoons PCl_5$, $K_c = [PCl_5] / ([PCl_3][Cl_2]) = (\text{mol dm}^{-3}) / ((\text{mol dm}^{-3})(\text{mol dm}^{-3})) = \text{mol}^{-1}\text{dm}^3$.

questions.question: At dynamic chemical equilibrium, which of the following statements is true? (FBISE 2023-II)

options.A: The forward and reverse reactions proceed at equal rates
options.B: The reaction stops completely and no molecular exchange occurs
options.C: The concentration of reactants must equal the concentration of products
options.D: The reaction can no longer be reversed

questions.explanation: Dynamic chemical equilibrium occurs when the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction, while both reactions continue indefinitely in a closed system.

questions.question: What is the characteristic color of iodine ($I_2$) vapor in the reversible synthesis of hydrogen iodide? (FBISE 2014-I, 2023-I)
questions.explanation: Iodine vapor has a distinctive purple/violet color. When it reacts reversibly with colorless hydrogen gas ($H_2$) to form colorless hydrogen iodide ($HI$), the purple intensity decreases until equilibrium is established.

questions.question: The numerical value of the equilibrium constant $K_c$ for a given chemical reaction depends primarily upon: (FBISE 2022-II)

options.A: Total volume of the reaction container

questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant $K_c$ is temperature-dependent. Changing pressure, volume, or concentrations changes the equilibrium position, but only temperature changes the actual value of $K_c$.

questions.question: Which gases are used as the reactants to manufacture ammonia in the Haber-Bosch process? (FBISE 2021-II)
questions.explanation: Ammonia ($NH_3$) is synthesized reversibly from nitrogen gas ($N_2$, from air) and hydrogen gas ($H_2$, from methane/natural gas) via $N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)$.

questions.question: What is the physical appearance/color of pure gaseous hydrogen iodide ($HI$)? (FBISE 2020-II)
questions.explanation: Hydrogen iodide ($HI$) is a colorless gas. When $HI$ decomposes upon heating into hydrogen and iodine, a purple color reappears due to free $I_2$ vapor.

questions.question: If the reaction quotient $Q_c$ is less than $K_c$ ($Q_c < K_c$), what is the net direction of the chemical reaction? (FBISE 2013-I, 2017-I, 2018-II, 2019-I, 2020-II)

options.C: The system is already at equilibrium

questions.explanation: When $Q_c < K_c$, the ratio of product concentration to reactant concentration is lower than at equilibrium. The reaction shifts from left to right (forward) to produce more products until $Q_c = K_c$.

questions.question: What is the standard SI unit of active mass / molar concentration? (FBISE 2018-II)
questions.explanation: Active mass is defined as the concentration of a substance in moles per cubic decimeter ($\text{mol dm}^{-3}$), represented by square brackets $[\ ]$.

questions.question: Reversible chemical reactions that contain comparable amounts of both reactants and products at dynamic equilibrium have: (FBISE 2017-II, 2020-I)
questions.explanation: A moderate $K_c$ value indicates that neither forward nor reverse reaction goes to completion, resulting in comparable equilibrium concentrations of both reactants and products.

questions.question: In an open lime kiln, the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate ($CaCO_3(s) \rightleftharpoons CaO(s) + CO_2(g)$) goes to completion because: (FBISE 2015-II, 2019-II)

options.B: $CO_2$ gas continuously escapes from the open vessel

questions.explanation: In an open kiln, the gaseous product $CO_2$ escapes continuously into the atmosphere. The reverse reaction cannot occur, driving the decomposition irreversibly to completion.

questions.question: A reverse reaction is best defined as a reaction in which: (FBISE 2013-II, 2019-I)

options.A: Reactants react to form products gradually
options.B: Products react together to reform original reactants
options.C: Reaction rate continuously slows down to zero

questions.explanation: In a reversible reaction, the reverse reaction is the process where newly formed products interact to regenerate the initial reactant molecules.

questions.question: At the very beginning of a reversible reaction ($t = 0$), the initial rate of the reverse reaction is: (FBISE 2018-II)
questions.explanation: At $t = 0$, only reactant molecules are present and product concentration is zero. Therefore, the rate of the reverse reaction is initially zero/negligible.

questions.question: When the reaction quotient equals the equilibrium constant ($Q_c = K_c$), the chemical system is: (FBISE 2017-II, 2018-I, 2019-II, 2020-I, 2021-I)
questions.explanation: When $Q_c = K_c$, the concentrations of reactants and products satisfy the equilibrium condition; the forward and reverse rates are exactly balanced.

questions.question: What is the equilibrium constant ($K_c$) unit for the synthesis of ammonia: $N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)$? (FBISE 2018-II)
For the formation of hydrogen iodide ($H_2(g) + I_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2HI(g)$), what is the unit of $K_c$? (FBISE 2016-I, 2022-I)
questions.explanation: Number of moles of reactants = $1 + 1 = 2$; number of moles of products = $2$. Since $\Delta n = 2 - 2 = 0$, concentration units cancel completely, making $K_c$ dimensionless.

questions.question: The Law of Mass Action was formulated by C.M. Guldberg and Peter Waage in the year: (FBISE 2015-I, 2023-II)
questions.explanation: Norwegian scientists Cato Maximilian Guldberg and Peter Waage proposed the Law of Mass Action in 1864, relating reaction rate directly to active masses of reacting substances.

questions.question: According to the Law of Mass Action, the rate of a chemical reaction is directly proportional to the product of: (FBISE 2017-I)

options.C: Active masses of the reacting substances

questions.explanation: The Law of Mass Action states that the rate of a chemical reaction is directly proportional to the product of the active masses (molar concentrations) of reacting substances raised to appropriate powers.

questions.question: What is the equilibrium constant expression for the hypothetical reaction $2A + B \rightleftharpoons 3C$? (FBISE 2025 Model)
questions.explanation: In an equilibrium expression, product concentrations appear in the numerator and reactant concentrations appear in the denominator, each raised to a power equal to its stoichiometric coefficient: $K_c = [C]^3 / ([A]^2[B])$.

questions.question: A chemical reaction having a very large equilibrium constant ($K_c \gg 10^3$) indicates that: (FBISE 2019-II)

options.A: The reaction proceeds to almost complete conversion into products
options.B: The reaction barely proceeds in the forward direction
options.C: Equilibrium consists almost entirely of original reactants
options.D: The reaction rate is exceedingly slow

questions.explanation: A very large value of $K_c$ means that at equilibrium, the concentration of products is far greater than that of reactants, indicating the forward reaction has gone almost to completion.

questions.question: A chemical reaction with an extremely small value of $K_c$ ($K_c \ll 10^{-3}$) implies that: (FBISE 2021-I)

options.A: Equilibrium mixture consists predominantly of products
options.C: The forward reaction barely takes place and reactants remain largely intact

questions.explanation: A very small $K_c$ value indicates that only an infinitesimal amount of reactants converts to products before equilibrium is reached; the mixture remains almost entirely reactants.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an irreversible reaction? (FBISE 2016-II)
questions.explanation: Combustion of hydrogen with oxygen to form water is an irreversible reaction that goes to completion; liquid water does not spontaneously dissociate back into hydrogen and oxygen under standard conditions.

questions.question: In a closed vessel containing $N_2O_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2(g)$, dinitrogen tetroxide is colorless while nitrogen dioxide is reddish-brown. If the mixture is compressed, Le Chatelier's principle predicts that the color will initially darken and then: (Conceptual)

options.B: Fade as the system shifts toward colorless $N_2O_4$

questions.explanation: Compression increases pressure. By Le Chatelier's principle, the system relieves pressure by shifting toward the side with fewer gas molecules (1 mole $N_2O_4$ vs 2 moles $NO_2$), thus fading to lighter color.

questions.question: Which macroscopic property remains constant once dynamic equilibrium is established in a closed container? (FBISE 2022-II)

options.C: Total kinetic energy of individual atoms

questions.explanation: At equilibrium, all measurable macroscopic properties such as concentration, total pressure, temperature, density, and color intensity remain constant because the rates of opposing reactions are equal.

questions.question: What role does a chemical catalyst play in a reversible reaction? (FBISE 2023-I)

options.B: Shifts the equilibrium position toward higher yield of product
options.C: Accelerates both forward and reverse rates equally to reach equilibrium faster
options.D: Slows down the reverse reaction selectively

questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy equally for both forward and reverse reactions. It allows equilibrium to be reached more rapidly without changing the equilibrium composition or the value of $K_c$.

questions.question: For the reaction $CO(g) + 2H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons CH_3OH(g)$, what is the unit of $K_c$?
questions.explanation: $K_c = [CH_3OH] / ([CO][H_2]^2) = (\text{mol dm}^{-3}) / ((\text{mol dm}^{-3})(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^2) = (\text{mol dm}^{-3})^{-2} = \text{mol}^{-2}\text{dm}^6$.

questions.question: Static equilibrium is most commonly observed in: (FBISE 2014-II)

options.A: Physical systems and stationary mechanical structures

questions.explanation: Static equilibrium occurs when a system completely ceases all motion and reactions (e.g., a building standing upright where balanced forces prevent any motion). In contrast, chemical equilibrium is always dynamic.

questions.question: When active mass is represented in chemical equations, it is enclosed in: (FBISE 2015-I)
questions.explanation: Molar concentrations (active masses in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$) are universally represented by surrounding the chemical formula with square brackets $[ \ ]$.

questions.question: If a reversible reaction has $K_c = 1.0$ at a specific temperature, what does this indicate about the equilibrium state?

options.A: Products and reactants exist in equal concentration products

questions.explanation: $K_c = [\text{Products}] / [\text{Reactants}] = 1.0$, which means that the concentration product in the numerator equals the concentration product in the denominator.

questions.question: For the reaction $2SO_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2SO_3(g)$, what is the unit of $K_c$?
Which of the following conditions is mandatory to establish dynamic chemical equilibrium?

options.A: An open container with continuous gas ventilation
options.B: A closed system at constant temperature
options.C: The presence of a platinum catalyst

questions.explanation: Dynamic chemical equilibrium can only be achieved in a closed system so that neither reactants nor products can escape, and at a constant temperature.

questions.question: When nitrogen dioxide ($NO_2$) gas is cooled, it dimerizes into dinitrogen tetroxide ($N_2O_4$). This dimerization reaction is exothermic ($2NO_2 \rightleftharpoons N_2O_4 + \text{heat}$). Decreasing temperature will:

options.A: Shift equilibrium toward colorless $N_2O_4$ and increase $K_c$
options.B: Shift equilibrium toward brown $NO_2$ and decrease $K_c$
options.C: Have no effect on the equilibrium position
options.D: Cause both gases to decompose into elements

questions.explanation: For an exothermic forward reaction, removing heat by cooling shifts the equilibrium to the right (toward products) according to Le Chatelier's principle, thus increasing $K_c$.

questions.question: In the reaction $H_2 + I_2 \rightleftharpoons 2HI$, if initial concentrations are $[H_2] = 0.1\text{ M}$, $[I_2] = 0.1\text{ M}$, and $[HI] = 0.4\text{ M}$, and $K_c = 49$, what is $Q_c$ and which way does the reaction move?
questions.explanation: $Q_c = [HI]^2 / ([H_2][I_2]) = (0.4)^2 / (0.1 \times 0.1) = 0.16 / 0.01 = 16$. Since $Q_c (16) < K_c (49)$, the reaction proceeds forward to produce more $HI$.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the equilibrium constant of the forward reaction ($K_c$) and the reverse reaction ($K_c'$)?
questions.explanation: Because the numerator and denominator swap when a chemical equation is written in reverse, the equilibrium constant of the reverse reaction is the mathematical reciprocal of the forward reaction ($K_c' = 1 / K_c$).

questions.question: Why does the rate of the forward reaction decrease as a reversible reaction proceeds toward equilibrium?

options.A: Concentration of reactants decreases over time
options.D: The temperature of the vessel drops continuously

questions.explanation: According to the Law of Mass Action, reaction rate is directly proportional to reactant concentrations. As reactants are consumed to form products, their concentrations decrease, slowing the forward rate.
